title: Staff Augmentation vs. Outsourcing: Which One Fits?
excerpt: Two ways to add engineering capacity, and how to choose between them.

author.name: Boyo Martínez
author.bio: Boyo leads product and design at NicaSource, where he helps US companies plan, staff and run nearshore engineering teams. He has spent fifteen years shipping digital products with distributed teams across the Americas.

meta.body:
Introduction

Staff augmentation and project outsourcing both add capacity, but they put control in very different places. Choosing the wrong one is an expensive lesson.

Staff Augmentation

You add engineers to your own team. You set priorities, run the rituals and own the architecture; the partner handles recruiting, payroll and retention.

Best when

  • You have product and engineering leadership in place.
  • The roadmap changes often and you need flexibility.
  • You want knowledge to stay inside your company.

Project Outsourcing

You hand over a defined scope. The partner manages the team and delivers against a contract.

Best when

  • The scope is stable and well documented.
  • The work is outside your core product.

If the work is core to your product, keep it inside your team, even when the people are not on your payroll.

Conclusion

Most growing product companies end up with augmentation for their core product and outsourcing for well-defined side projects. Know which is which before you sign.
